publications.title: FrogNet field probe publishes a bounded research contract
publications.summary: The public prerelease documents a conservative frog-present ranking head, its checked runtime format, field threshold, provenance, and unsupported uses.

sections.heading: What was released
sections.body: FrogNet field probe v0.1.0 is a conservative binary frog-present head for 1,536-dimensional Google Perch 2 embeddings. The release describes three non-overlapping five-second embeddings per 15-second recording and a checked JSON/NPZ runtime bundle.

sections.heading: What the score means
sections.body: The release defines its output as an uncalibrated case-control ranking score and names a conservative field threshold of 0.95. It does not turn a threshold crossing into a confirmed animal observation.

sections.heading: What remains bounded
sections.body: The public package excludes private field evidence. The release must be read with its smoke tests, provenance, limitations, and unsupported-use statements rather than as a general field-validity claim.

publications.title: Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 makes scale explicit
publications.summary: NASA's HLS project provides global land-surface reflectance at 30-meter resolution every two to three days, useful context only when a field comparison preserves the difference in scale and measured quantity.
publications.evidence_state: external dataset context; no local comparison result

sections.heading: What the project provides
sections.body: NASA describes Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 as global land-surface reflectance data produced every two to three days at 30-meter resolution.

sections.heading: Why it is relevant here
sections.body: That cadence and spatial grain can provide landscape context for field work, but a shared date does not make a local sensor and a satellite pixel equivalent measurements.

sections.heading: What remains separate
sections.body: No Pine Hollow observation, causal relationship, occupancy estimate, or cross-scale validation is asserted in this review record.

publications.title: An open acoustic build should preserve the tool boundary
publications.summary: BirdNET-Analyzer is an MIT-licensed open repository for scientific audio processing; a field build should name the upstream tool, local wrapper, evidence boundary, and failure behavior separately.
publications.evidence_state: software context; not a Pine Hollow detection claim

sections.heading: The upstream tool
sections.body: The canonical BirdNET-Analyzer repository describes itself as an analyzer for scientific audio data processing and publishes its code under the MIT license.

sections.heading: The field-system boundary
sections.body: A serviceable build should distinguish upstream analysis software from local capture, scheduling, review, storage, and publication layers.

sections.heading: The evidence boundary
sections.body: BirdNET remains an independent evidence lane at Pine Hollow. Its output is not silently merged with specialist Vortex model assertions or human review decisions.

publications.title: Correction records preserve the wording that changed
publications.summary: A review-only demonstration of append-only correction metadata; it does not describe an external factual error or released Vortex claim.

sections.heading: Revision one
sections.body: The demonstration initially described a source as updated daily.

sections.heading: Revision two
sections.body: The wording was replaced with source-timestamp language because update cadence must come from the source record rather than editorial shorthand.

sections.heading: Why the prior wording remains visible
sections.body: A correction is a new revision with a reason and timestamp, not a silent replacement of the historical record.

corrections.summary: Replaced an unsupported daily-cadence phrase with source-timestamp language.

publications.title: NASA-led study tests SAR mapping of tornado damage tracks
publications.summary: NASA Earthdata reported that a study led by NASA researchers used Sentinel-1A synthetic aperture radar coherence data to identify five of nine surveyed tornado tracks from Tennessee's March 2020 outbreak. The method supplemented comparison with National Weather Service radar data and ground damage surveys; it did not detect the study's EF0 tracks.
publications.related_program: Earth observation and conservation-oriented field systems
publications.evidence_level: Official NASA Earthdata report of a bounded remote-sensing study
publications.evidence_state: External research result reported by NASA Earthdata; candidate pending editorial claim, privacy, and rights review

sections.heading: What changed
sections.body: NASA Earthdata published an August 7, 2026 account of a study led by NASA researchers that paired before-and-after Sentinel-1A synthetic aperture radar observations and analyzed low-coherence linear features as possible tornado tracks. Five of nine well-surveyed Tennessee tracks were detectable in the SAR imagery; tracks longer than 10 kilometers and rated EF2 or higher were easiest to identify, while no EF0 tracks were detectable.

sections.heading: Why it matters here
sections.body: The work is a concrete Earth-observation method for supplementing field assessment where terrain, weather, access, or event scale complicate ground surveys. It is relevant to Vortex work on multi-modal field systems because it shows how a satellite change-detection layer can be compared with established ground and radar evidence rather than treated as a stand-alone observation.

sections.heading: What remains separate
sections.body: This was a retrospective study of nine tornado tracks from one Tennessee outbreak, not a Pine Hollow observation or a Vortex deployment. SAR did not identify every surveyed track, and the reported method supplements rather than replaces National Weather Service damage surveys. Use of this public NASA report and the referenced satellite data does not imply NASA affiliation, participation, funding, or partnership for the Vortex Project.

sources.title: Tracing a Tornado’s Path of Destruction

review_assessment.claims_basis: NASA Earthdata supports the Sentinel-1A SAR method, five-of-nine detection result, stronger detectability for tracks longer than 10 km and rated EF2 or higher, and non-detection of EF0 tracks. The Dispatch preserves the retrospective scope, bounded sample, limitations, NWS evidence boundary, and no-affiliation statement.
review_assessment.privacy_basis: The public derivative contains no Pine Hollow coordinates, private paths or hosts, credentials, private IP addresses, personal information, raw media, or unpublished Pine Hollow evidence.
review_assessment.rights_basis: The Dispatch uses original Vortex summary and section text, an attributed authoritative source link, and no copied NASA image, audio, video, logo, or long quotation.

publication_approval.basis: Accountable human approved the exact reviewed revision after recorded claim, privacy, and rights checks.
